title: Build a Keycloak client that matches its runtime
description: Select an application shape, then change Keycloak capability settings and watch the trust boundary pass or fail.

profiles.label: Server web application
profiles.summary: The backend handles the callback and can protect client credentials.
profiles.tokenLocation: Encrypted server-side session or token store
requiredControls: Protect the client credential in a secret manager or workload identity boundary.
Bind state, nonce, redirect URI, code, and PKCE verifier to one browser transaction.
Give the browser only a hardened application session cookie where feasible.

profiles.label: Single-page application
profiles.summary: Browser JavaScript is a public client and cannot protect a shared secret.
profiles.tokenLocation: Prefer a backend-for-frontend; otherwise keep browser exposure narrow
requiredControls: Require Authorization Code with PKCE S256.
Register exact HTTPS callbacks and narrow web origins.
Keep Implicit flow and Direct access grants disabled.

profiles.label: Native application
profiles.summary: Installed code is a public client even when reverse engineering is inconvenient.
requiredControls: Open authorization in an external user-agent.
Require PKCE S256 and a platform-appropriate exact callback.
Do not package a shared client secret in the application.

profiles.label: Machine service
profiles.summary: A confidential workload requests access on its own behalf without a browser user.
profiles.tokenLocation: Workload memory; credential in a protected secret or key boundary
requiredControls: Enable Client authentication and Service account roles.
Assign only the service-account roles required by the workload.
Disable browser login and Direct access grants for this client.
